$comment: What this LAUNCHER installs, and what a check may believe about it.
`checked` is proved against this repository by scripts/manifest-is-true.sh;
`declared` is a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THIS FILE ANSWERS THE OTHER HALF OF THE QUESTION. Sixteen repositories now
declare what they BUILD. A launcher builds nothing, so its manifest declares
what it INSTALLS, the way TAIPANBOX/taipan's does.
AND THERE IS ALREADY A SECOND OPINION, WHICH IS THE POINT. estate-gates' C5
works out the same list by PARSING this repository from a central file: it
greps `register <name>` out of up.sh and equivalents out of the other two
launchers' quite different syntaxes. That parser is careful and it is still
somebody else's reading of our source. Now there are two independent
statements of one fact, each able to catch the other drifting, and the check
below is this side of it: the list here is compared against up.sh and
routines.sh in the repository that owns them.
THE THREE LISTS ARE NOT ONE LIST. A supervised service, a Python tool
installed into a venv and a scheduled routine are installed three different
ways here, and flattening them would lose exactly the distinction an
operator needs. `mockryx-drill` is in `routines` and in no other list,
because this launcher schedules mockryx without supervising it.
PROFILES ARE OPT-IN AND LISTED SEPARATELY. `--with-delegation` brings up
vouchryx and `--with-finops` brings up costcrew; both appear in `services`
because the question that list answers is what this launcher CAN bring up,
not what a default run does. `routines_by_default` is the narrower answer
for the scheduled half, and it is smaller than `routines` on purpose.
distribution: git clone and ./up.sh (./down.sh, ./routines.sh) on one machine; builds every plane from source at whatever commit it finds, pinning no released image or tag

it_is_the_sandbox_and_that_changes_defau.why: Several values here differ from the two server deployments on purpose and are recorded in estate-gates' deployment-parity file rather than here: HERALDYX_MIN_SEVERITY is `medium` where they use `high`, there is no console and no policy database. A launcher's manifest says what it installs; whether that agrees with the others is C5's question.

mockryx_is_scheduled_and_not_supervised.why: It appears in `schedules_routines` and in no other list. A drill runs and exits, so there is no process to register, and it is opt-in everywhere, which is why it is absent from routines_by_default too.

typryx_journal_joins_the_shared_bus.value: $STACK_UP_HOME/events/typryx.ndjson; the ledger stays on its own path, $STACK_UP_HOME/typryx/ledger
typryx_journal_joins_the_shared_bus.why: @decided 2026-09-26: agent-passport SPEC 6.2 (agent-passport#67) registers typryx's four event types (typed_answer, typed_unanswered, typed_refused, calibration_drift) in the estate's own event schema, so the earlier reason for keeping this journal off the shared bus (an unregistered source trailryx-seal's *.ndjson import would pick up blind) no longer holds. TYPRYX_BACKEND is stub here unless the operator chose a data mode (see typed_data_mode_is_chosen_not_defaulted): free, deterministic, no outbound call.
typryx_journal_joins_the_shared_bus.note: @claude 2026-09-26: registered is not the same as sealed. typryx emits schema agent-event/v1.0, which trailryx-agentevent does not accept yet (it reads v0.1 through v0.3), so trailryx-seal refuses every line here for unknown_schema before it ever inspects the event type; measured 2026-09-26 against this launcher's own run. The practical outcome is the one roughly forty other unmapped or unrecognized event types already get on this bus: counted, not sealed. Moving the journal here only stops it being an unregistered source; it does not make trailryx seal it.

tokenfuse_mcp_broker_fronts_typryx_by_co.value: tokenfuse's own `mcp-broker` subcommand, TOKENFUSE_MCP_UPSTREAM(S) pointed at typryx's :4320/mcp
tokenfuse_mcp_broker_fronts_typryx_by_co.why: @decided 2026-09-26: tokenfuse's code is not changed for this. `up.sh` already builds the tokenfuse binary for the money plane; --with-typed reuses that same binary's `mcp-broker` subcommand and points it at typryx through its documented environment contract alone (TOKENFUSE_MCP_UPSTREAM(S), TOKENFUSE_MCP_KEYS, TOKENFUSE_MCP_SECRETS, TOKENFUSE_MCP_SECRET_SCOPES). A brokered call resolves its typryx credential from `params._meta` (typryx#6, TYPRYX_ACCEPT_KEY_IN_META=1 here) because the broker forwards a tools/call with no header of its own.

typed_data_mode_is_chosen_not_defaulted.value: --typed-mode jev | own-model | off; unset keeps today's behaviour (nothing without --with-typed, the stub backend with it)
typed_data_mode_is_chosen_not_defaulted.why: @decided 2026-09-30: a customer chooses where typed-answer data goes. jev sends the named fields of each question to TypeSafe AI's hosted API and takes its key from a file named by --typed-key-file, never from an environment value; own-model points typryx at the customer's own OpenAI-compatible server (--typed-model-url ending in /v1, --typed-model, optional key file) so nothing leaves their hardware; off starts nothing. Refusals happen at argument parsing, before any build, and --typed-plan prints the resolved choice without starting anything. The launcher never reads the key file's bytes; typryx does.
typed_data_mode_is_chosen_not_defaulted.note: @claude 2026-09-30: TYPRYX_TRAINING_DIR is wired by the separate flag in typed_training_log_is_opt_in; it is typryx v0.3.0 and newer, and this launcher builds from source at whatever it finds, so the flag checks the built typryx can log before it starts one.

typed_training_log_is_opt_in.value: --typed-training (off by default) sets TYPRYX_TRAINING_DIR=$STACK_UP_HOME/typryx/training, created 0700, beside the ledger at $STACK_UP_HOME/typryx/ledger; needs typryx to run and typryx v0.3.0 or newer
typed_training_log_is_opt_in.why: @decided 2026-09-30: a customer can train a model of their own on their own questions and their own human judgements, and typryx supplies the records, so the training log is an opt-in kept off unless asked for. The log holds the question fields a template lets through and never a backend's answer, and the export (typryx export --training) takes its labels from human truths posted to /v1/outcome only, so a hosted provider's answers never become training labels through it. Nothing in this launcher reads or sends the log.
